title: Pressure-Guard: Emergency runtime mitigation for cross-environment KV handle retention and slab allocator drift causing intermittent GPU OOMs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported recurrent GPU OOMs over a 10–48 hour window under mixed short/long sequence workloads. Investigation identified two interacting root causes: (1) stale KV handles retained during session handoffs leading to effective KV-cache leaks, and (2) slab allocator drift/fragmentation under mixed allocation sizes that prevented reclamation under pressure. Together these caused long-tail memory pressure that only surfaced under high-concurrency multi-tenant Dedicated pools and specific Hosted traffic shapes.

Impact: Intermittent OOMs caused degraded latency and dropped sessions for multiple customers (see incident INC-2025-0027). For Dedicated customers this correlated with increased customer support tickets and one escalated account (enterprise tier) requesting immediate mitigation.

Work done so far: triage, reproducer, and emergency patch. We implemented a short-term runtime hotpatch (pressure-guard) that: (A) enforces deterministic KV handle ownership transfer during session handoff (coarse-grained epoch-based ownership) to avoid transient retention, (B) adds a forced tombstone sweep path when observed KV handle counts exceed a safety threshold, and (C) enables a lightweight background slab compaction heuristic that triggers at configurable pressure levels to reduce fragmentation without pausing inference. Patch is implemented as runtime changes + config flags guarded behind a canary rollout.

Risks and trade-offs: The epoch-based handle transfer avoids complex per-handle refcounts and minimizes perf cost, but may delay immediate reclamation by one epoch window under extreme churn. Background compaction trades a small amount of CPU/GPU driver interaction for reduced allocation pressure; we tuned it conservatively to avoid spikes. The forced tombstone sweep increases short-term I/O/CPU cost during sweeps; we rate-limit sweeps and add observability to revert if adverse.

Next steps / Rollout plan: 1) Internal QA + stress tests (24–48h), 2) Canary rollout to 5% of Hosted API (low-risk), 3) Canary to one Dedicated pool (non-critical customer) and one Private test cluster, 4) Monitor for 72h, expand to 50% then full if stable. Canary includes automatic fallback to compatible model variant (lower memory) on nodes that hit pressure thresholds.

Acceptance criteria: No repeat of the incident pattern (looking for >95% reduction in OOM events over 72h in canary), bounded increase in CPU <5% and no visible regression in p50/p95 latency for generation.

Follow-ups: postmortem, add e2e eviction tests to CI, refine slab allocator heuristics for heterogeneous allocation patterns, explore stronger KV handle invariants for long term rewrite.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Asha Patel: Initial pagertriage. Noticed correlation with session handoff paths and large mixed-sequence workloads. Reproducer attached: reproducer/oom-multi-tenant-2025.tar.gz (uploaded to incident ticket). Created ENG-94231 for emergency patching.

2025-02-19 - Marco Ruiz: Added heap inspector traces and GPU mem maps from affected nodes (s3://redwood-logs/INC-2025-0027/). Found stale kv_handle refs surviving handoff during preemptive session-swaps. Started spike on epoch-ownership design. Draft PR created.

2025-02-20 - Leah Chen (SRE): Ran chaos test against dedicated pool with 200 concurrent sessions; reproduced OOM after ~18 hours. Confirmed fragmentation patterns consistent across GPUs when churn > 30k allocations/minute.

2025-02-22 - Marco Ruiz: Submitted runtime hotpatch PR for pressure-guard: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289. Contains: epoch ownership transfer, tombstone sweep path, background compactor. Unit + integration tests added.

2025-02-23 - Sophie Blake (PM): Notified affected customers with temporary mitigation advice (reduce per-session context length, scale dedicated pool horizontally). Customers accepted canary testing for faster rollout.

2025-02-25 - Code review (Dmitri Ivanov): Reviewed PR, suggested changing compaction backoff to exponential and adding metrics for sweep duration and reclaimed bytes. Marked ready-for-canary after updates.

2025-02-27 - Marco Ruiz: Canary started at 5% hosted, one dedicated pool and one private cluster. Early telemetry: 70% reduction in OOM signals on canary nodes in first 12h. No latency regressions observed.
2025-03-03 - Asha Patel: Patch in In Review; documenting postmortem template and follow-ups. Preparing rollout to 50% if no regressions in next 48h.
